paragraphs.source_en:
Destructions] Agents of destruction: OED 1 d cites Scott, The Lady of the Lake III xi: ‘Quench thou
his light, Destruction dark!’
 peers or] peers & Ashley. spies] At the Home Office, Sidmouth oversaw a network of government
informers and spies who operated throughout the country and reported to him on radical activity for
reform. The spies, who sometimes acted more like agents provocateurs, were widely despised. See notes
to PB3 (Longman iii 70–152) 152, 671.
 ‘And I looked, and behold a pale horse; and his name that sat on him was Death and Hell fol-
lowed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword,
and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth’ (Revelation vi 7). Rossetti 1870
noticed the discrepancy between S.’s pale Death and the Bible’s ‘pale horse’. Despite the comma in both
Ashley and LC, it remains ambiguous whether it is Anarchy or the horse that is splashed with blood.
